# polytype

`polytype` is a type projection tool for Go. It reads Go types statically at
`go generate` time, lowers them into one closed, validated type grammar
(package `typegrammar`), and projects that grammar into the other type systems
a program speaks. The Go type is the single source of truth; nothing uses
runtime reflection, and every projection refuses a shape it cannot represent
faithfully instead of widening to `any`.

Projections:

- JSON Schema for LLM tool definitions and structured output, embedded in Go
  (`go tool polytype`; always on). Properties follow Go field order, unknown
  properties are rejected, doc comments become descriptions.
- Validation methods over those schemas (`--validate`; `--formats=both` adds
  YAML input through `go.yaml.in/yaml/v4`, translated to the JSON data model).
- Go JSON codecs inferred from the types: membership-checked enums,
  discriminated sealed unions, YAML adapters. No flag selects them.
- Structural TypeScript declarations (`--typescript DIR`, or package
  `typescript` from a Go program that already knows its roots).
- devalue transport: a Go port of the devalue runtime SvelteKit uses, plus
  generated strict Go encoders/decoders for your types on that wire
  (packages `devalue` and `devalue/codegen`).
- Your own backend: load a package and lower any roots into the grammar
  (package `grammar`), then walk the nodes.

JSON is the canonical data model and the default format. The default union
discriminator property is `type` in every projection.

Repository: https://github.com/tylergannon/polytype
Human documentation: https://go-gen-jsonschema.tylergannon.com

## Recommended setup

Use Go's tool directive so the generator version is pinned in `go.mod` and is
the same for developers and CI:

```bash
go get -tool github.com/tylergannon/polytype/polytype@latest
```

Define the types and generation command:

```go
// types.go
package contacts

import "github.com/tylergannon/polytype"

//go:generate go tool polytype --validate --formats=both

// Person is a contact extracted from a document.
type Person struct {
    // Full legal name.
    Name string `json:"name"`

    // Email address. Omit when the source does not provide one.
    Email polytype.Optional[string] `json:"email,omitzero"`

    // Required key; null means no phone number was supplied.
    Phone polytype.Nullable[string] `json:"phone"`
}
```

Write the build-tagged registration file by hand. It holds one panic stub
per generated method and one `Declare` line per root type:

```go
// schema.go
//go:build jsonschema

package contacts

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "github.com/tylergannon/polytype"
)

func (Person) Schema() json.RawMessage     { panic("not implemented") }
func (Person) ValidateJSON(_ []byte) error { panic("not implemented") }
func (Person) ValidateYAML(_ []byte) error { panic("not implemented") }

var _ = polytype.Declare(Person.Schema)
```

The stubs exist only so the package compiles under the `jsonschema` tag
while the generator runs. Write a `ValidateJSON` stub when the directive
passes `--validate` and a `ValidateYAML` stub when it also passes
`--formats=both`.

Generate:

```bash
go generate ./...
go mod tidy
```

Run `go mod tidy` when generation adds dependencies. Validation imports
`github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`; opted-in YAML support imports
`go.yaml.in/yaml/v4`.

Generation writes:

- `jsonschema/Person.json`: the schema;
- `jsonschema/Person.json.sum`: its change-detection checksum; and
- `jsonschema_gen.go`: production schema, validation, and selected codec
  implementations.

Commit `schema.go`, `jsonschema_gen.go`, and the complete `jsonschema/`
directory.

Use `Person{}.Schema()` to obtain the embedded schema as `json.RawMessage` for a
tool definition or structured-output request.

## TypeScript declaration output

Pass `--typescript DIR` to generate structural TypeScript declarations in
`DIR/types.ts` alongside the ordinary JSON Schema and Go outputs. Relative
directories are resolved from the command's invocation directory, independently
of `--target`; absolute paths also work. Add `--typescript-barrel` to generate
an `index.ts` with explicit type-only exports from `./types.js`:

```go
//go:generate go tool polytype --typescript web/src/generated --typescript-barrel
```

```ts
// web/src/app.ts
import type { Person } from "./generated/index.js";
```

The generator only replaces files carrying its generated-file header. It
refuses to overwrite an application-owned `types.ts` or `index.ts`. A later run
without `--typescript-barrel` removes a generated `index.ts` and preserves an
application-owned one.

This output is for static structural checking. It does not provide runtime
decoding or validation on the JSON wire; issue #71 tracks that proof, and the
devalue codecs (below) are the typed, runtime-checked Go/JavaScript transport
polytype ships. Time values remain strings and
numeric fields become `number`, so TypeScript does not enforce Go integer ranges
or JSON Schema formats. Enum literals that cannot be represented exactly are
rejected. Runtime schema providers, custom JSON/text codecs, and other
unsupported static shapes fail generation rather than widening to `any` or
`unknown`. Production generation has no Node, npm, or JavaScript-engine
dependency.

To adopt declarations with the generated Go JSON boundary, pin one explicit
module release for both the tool and imported marker/runtime package, then use a
single directive:

```bash
go get -tool github.com/tylergannon/polytype/polytype@v1.0.0-rc.10
```

The `devalue`, `devalue/codegen`, and `grammar` packages require `v1.0.0-rc.10` or newer; the `typescript` package requires the release after it. The combined TypeScript and codec surface requires `v1.0.0-rc.8` or newer: `v1.0.0-rc.4` includes
TypeScript declarations but predates generated owner codecs, and releases before
`v1.0.0-rc.7` predate the marker-based enum and sealed-union registration. Pin
the version explicitly.

```go
//go:generate go tool polytype --validate --typescript web/src/generated --typescript-barrel
```

`--typescript-barrel` is optional. Sealed interface fields and `.StringerEnum`
registrations automatically cause the containing struct's JSON methods to be
generated; there is no codec flag. Run `go generate ./...` and `go mod tidy`,
then commit the schema, Go, and requested TypeScript outputs together. Encode
the containing Go struct with `json.Marshal`. For incoming bytes, call its
generated `ValidateJSON` before `json.Unmarshal`.

TypeScript uses the generated declarations with the platform's
`JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify`; the generator emits no TypeScript runtime decoder
or validator. Type annotations do not validate untrusted runtime input, so the
application must validate that boundary. Issue #71 owns the broader executed
JavaScript transport proof and does not turn these declarations into runtime
codecs.

A Go program that already knows which types it wants can skip the CLI and its
schema outputs: `github.com/tylergannon/polytype/typescript` is the same
backend as a library. See "Library entry points" and "Driving polytype from
another generator" below.

## Build-tag model

The registration and generated files are mutually exclusive:

| File | Build tag | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema.go` | `//go:build jsonschema` | User-written stubs and registrations, compiled only during generation. |
| `jsonschema_gen.go` | `//go:build !jsonschema` | Generated production accessors, validation, and selected codec methods. |

The package therefore has one definition of each generated method in either
build mode.

## Generated schema contract

- Properties are emitted in Go struct field order.
- `additionalProperties` is `false` for generated objects.
- Type and field doc comments become `description` values.
- Nested structs are inlined by default, unless registered with `.Ref()`
  (see "Shared definitions" below).
- Ordinary fields and `Nullable[T]` fields are required.
- Only `Optional[T]` removes a property from `required`.

For the `Person` example, `required` is `['name', 'phone']`; `email` remains a
property but is not required.

## Required, optional, and nullable properties

| Go field type | JSON property contract |
| --- | --- |
| `T` | Required and non-null. |
| `polytype.Optional[T]` | May be absent; rejects JSON null. |
| `polytype.Nullable[T]` | Required; accepts JSON null. |

`Optional[T]` fields must use `json:",omitzero"`. Their zero value represents
absence. A present zero, empty string, or empty slice is preserved through the
wrapper's `Present` and `Value` fields.

`Nullable[T]` uses `Present == false` for JSON null. Plain `json.Unmarshal`
cannot distinguish a missing nullable property from an explicit null, so call
generated `ValidateJSON` before unmarshaling whenever required-key presence
matters.

Do not use `omitempty` to express schema optionality. It affects Go marshaling,
not schema requiredness, and can remove a property that the schema requires.
The legacy `jsonschema:"optional"` tag is no longer honored; migrate the field
to `polytype.Optional[T]` with `json:",omitzero"`.

Supported wrapper shapes:

- `Optional`: scalars and named scalars, structs, pointers, arrays and slices,
  supported explicit references, and registered interface fields.
- `Nullable`: scalars, registered enums, structs, pointers to structs, and
  structs registered with `.Ref()`.

Wrappers must be the complete type of a direct named struct field. Aliases,
defined wrapper types, embedding, nesting, wrappers inside containers, and
unsupported Nullable shapes fail generation with an error.

OpenAI strict Structured Outputs requires every property to be required. Use
`Nullable[T]` for a required-plus-null contract. `Optional[T]` is intentionally
not compatible with that strict requirement.

## Validate before unmarshaling

Pass `--validate` to the generation directive and write a `ValidateJSON`
stub in the tagged file. Generated schemas are compiled once during package initialization. With
`--formats=both`, `ValidateYAML` translates YAML to the same JSON data model
before applying the schema.

```go
if err := (Person{}).ValidateJSON(llmOutput); err != nil {
    // Schema-validation failures can be inspected as
    // *jsonschemav6.ValidationError from
    // github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6. Malformed JSON may instead
    // return a parsing error.
    return err
}

var person Person
if err := json.Unmarshal(llmOutput, &person); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

Validation checks required fields, value types, unknown properties, enum
membership, discriminated union structure, and nested objects. Validation must
come first when schema validity and Go decoding have different information,
such as missing versus null Nullable fields.

## Schema descriptions

Type and field doc comments are copied into the JSON Schema. Write them as
instructions for the model producing JSON: define semantics, formats, units,
ranges, and when an Optional field should be omitted.

```go
// Time the event occurred, formatted as RFC3339, for example
// "2026-07-09T14:00:00Z".
Timestamp string `json:"timestamp"`
```

Use a `description:"..."` struct tag to override the doc comment in the
generated schema.

## Struct tags

| Tag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `json:"name"` | Sets the property name using standard Go JSON-tag rules. |
| `json:",omitzero"` | Required on `Optional[T]` so an absent wrapper is omitted. |
| `description:"..."` | Overrides the field doc comment in the schema. |
| `jsonschema:"ref=definitions/T"` | Emits an explicit `$ref`; the referenced schema must be defined by the consumer. |

## Enums

Enum-ness is a property of the type. A named type declares itself as an enum
with the marker method `func (T) enum() {}` in ordinary Go; its typed
constants in the same package become the enum values wherever the type is
used, with no field-level declaration:

```go
type Status string

func (Status) enum() {}

const (
    StatusPending Status = "pending"
    StatusDone    Status = "done"
)

type Task struct {
    Status Status `json:"status"`
}

var _ = polytype.Declare(Task.Schema)
```

The marker must be exactly `func (T) enum()`; a pointer receiver, another
signature, or a marked type with no typed constants fails generation naming
the type. The generated file references each marked type through its first
typed constant, as `var _ interface{ enum() } = StatusPending` (a value of the
marked type, not a pointer, since the marker has a value receiver), so the
marker counts as used by staticcheck; a package with marked enums but no
generation adds one such line per marked type by hand. The marker means value mode and ignores any `String()` method. A
marked integer type emits its raw numeric constant values; `.StringerEnum` on
a field emits constant names such as `LogDebug` and `LogInfo` as strings
instead (never the return values of `String()`).

Migration: `.Enum(field)`, `WithEnum(field)`, and the package-level
`NewEnumType[T]()` are removed; add `func (T) enum() {}` next to the type.
`.StringerEnum`/`WithStringerEnum` are unchanged.

Every marked enum type declared in the generation target package receives a
type-level value-receiver `MarshalJSON` and pointer-receiver `UnmarshalJSON`
that enforce membership in both directions: a value that is not a declared
constant fails to encode or decode with an error naming the enum type and the
value, and `null` is rejected. Marked enums imported from another package are
not guarded. A production JSON method already declared on a marked type fails
generation before any file is written.

String-mode integer fields generate one composed owner codec for encoding and
decoding, shared with any union adapters. Marshal the containing owner value
or pointer; a global enum method is not installed. Direct `E`, `Optional[E]`,
and `Nullable[E]` are supported. Optional absence and Nullable null skip the
conversion; present values must have a declared name. Unknown names,
undeclared values/zero, duplicate underlying values with distinct names,
production enum JSON hooks, and other adapted containers are rejected.
Other fields of the same marked integer type retain numeric JSON.
Registered enum fields cannot use `json:",string"`; generation rejects that
option before writing artifacts because its encoding differs from the schema.


## Discriminated interfaces and slices

A field whose type is a **sealed interface** becomes an `anyOf` union of the
interface's variants, discriminated by a `"type"` property whose value defaults
to the PascalCase concrete type name. An interface is sealed when its own body declares an
unexported method; its variants are inferred: every named struct type in the
same package that declares that method directly. The receiver of the sealing
method decides the variant kind: a value receiver is a value variant, a
pointer receiver is a pointer variant, and decoding constructs the variant
accordingly. Nothing is declared at the field. A direct one-dimensional slice
of the interface becomes an array with the union under `items.anyOf`. The generator writes owner `MarshalJSON` and `UnmarshalJSON` methods by default. Use
`--formats=both` to add `UnmarshalYAML(*yaml.Node)` adapters. yaml/v4 parses
YAML into a generic value, which is translated to JSON and passed through the
same decoder for scalar interface fields and every slice element.

```go
type Event interface{ isEvent() }

type Created struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
}
func (Created) isEvent() {}

type Deleted struct {
    ID string `json:"id"`
}
func (*Deleted) isEvent() {}

type Batch struct {
    Events []Event `json:"events"`
}
```

Nothing is declared at the field:

```go
var _ = polytype.Declare(Batch.Schema)
```

The discriminator value defaults to the concrete type name (`"Created"`,
`"Deleted"`) and the default discriminator property is `type` for both JSON and YAML.
Rejected with a diagnostic naming the type or field: a reachable field of a
non-sealed interface (no fallback), a sealing method obtained by embedding, a
type satisfying the interface only through an embedded field (excluded), a
direct candidate that does not implement the complete interface, zero
variants, an embedded interface payload, and a payload property colliding
with the discriminator. Renaming a variant type changes its wire value;
adding a qualifying implementation changes membership. Generated decoding preserves value versus pointer
implementations, reports a failing slice index, and assigns the destination
only after the entire value decodes successfully. YAML uses the JSON Schema
property names. Go `yaml` struct tags are ignored and nested custom
`UnmarshalYAML` hooks are bypassed; JSON tags and custom `UnmarshalJSON` hooks
are authoritative. The generator owns `UnmarshalYAML` on registered types.
yaml/v4 does not pass decoder options into that hook, so
`yaml.WithKnownFields()` cannot enforce strict fields inside a registered type;
use generated `ValidateYAML` for schema-backed unknown-property rejection.
Decoding is transactional replacement, so omitted YAML fields do not retain
receiver values. Use `yaml.WithV4Defaults()` to match `ValidateYAML` resolution.

Enable both formats in the generation directive before decoding YAML:

```go
//go:generate go tool polytype --formats=both
```

After generation, ordinary pipeline YAML can be decoded with yaml/v4:

```go
import yaml "go.yaml.in/yaml/v4"

var batch Batch
err := yaml.Load([]byte(`
events:
  - type: Created
    name: first
  - type: Deleted
    id: old-id
`), &batch, yaml.WithV4Defaults())
```

Run `go mod tidy` after YAML-enabled generation so the module records its
`go.yaml.in/yaml/v4` dependency.

The discriminator property is a property of the union. To use a property other
than `type`, declare it once in the build-tagged file of the package that
declares the interface: `var _ = polytype.SealedUnion[Event]("kind")`. Add
`polytype.Snake` or `polytype.Camel` as the optional second argument to inflect
the concrete type names; `polytype.Pascal` is the default. Executable
configuration passed to `codegen` may supply any non-nil `func(string) string`.
Every use of `Event` then shares the property and resolved values. The property
argument must be a nonempty string literal; a declaration in another package,
a duplicate, a non-sealed or non-interface target, or a payload collision with
the declared name fails generation naming the interface.

Migration: `.Interface(...)`, `WithInterface`, `WithInterfaceImpls`,
`WithDiscriminator`, `Impl`, `Discriminator`, and `NewInterfaceImpl[I]` are
removed; seal the interface, delete the field-level declaration, and move a
custom discriminator to `SealedUnion[I](name, inflector?)`.

Marshal the containing value with `json.Marshal(batch)` or
`json.Marshal(&batch)`. Its generated owner codec injects each field's
registered discriminator and preserves pointer/value implementation identity
through decoding. A concrete implementation marshaled outside its owner uses
its normal Go encoding; it has no global discriminator configuration.

Absent `Optional[I]` fields are omitted; allocated empty `[]I` fields encode
as `[]`. Nil required interfaces/slices, typed-nil implementations, present
Optional nil values return errors. A concrete
custom `MarshalJSON` hook must return an object; a missing discriminator is
added, a matching string is preserved, and conflicting/non-string values are
rejected. Concrete decode hooks receive the complete discriminated object.

Production owner `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` collisions, including competing
promoted methods, fail generation before writes. Generated owner decoding
replaces the destination only after full success; validate first when accepting
external JSON. See `examples/sealed_interface_slices` for roundtrip proof.

Supported interface containers are scalar `I` fields and direct `[]I` fields.
Fixed arrays, nested slices, named slice containers, `Optional[[]I]`,
`Nullable[[]I]`, and inline interface declarations are rejected. An
`Optional[I]` scalar field is supported; a `Nullable[I]` field is not.

## Shared definitions (`$ref`/`$defs`) via `Ref`

By default a type referenced from multiple places is inlined at every call
site. Add the zero-arg `.Ref()` option to that type's own registration to
render it once as `"$ref": "#/$defs/TypeName"` wherever another registered
schema references it instead:

```go
type Shared struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
}

type Container struct {
    Primary Shared   `json:"primary"`
    Others  []Shared `json:"others"`
}

var _ = polytype.Declare(Shared.Schema).Ref()
var _ = polytype.Declare(Container.Schema)
```

`Nullable` can wrap a `.Ref()` struct or registered enum. Both properties
remain required; their schemas become `anyOf` unions with JSON null, and the
referenced struct remains in `$defs`:

```go
type Mode string

const (
    ModeFast Mode = "fast"
    ModeSafe Mode = "safe"
)

type NullableConfig struct {
    Mode   polytype.Nullable[Mode]   `json:"mode"`
    Shared polytype.Nullable[Shared] `json:"shared"`
}

var _ = polytype.Declare(NullableConfig.Schema)
```

Migration: `NewJSONSchemaMethod(Shared.Schema, AsRef())` is now
`Declare(Shared.Schema).Ref()`. The legacy `NewJSONSchemaMethod`/
`NewJSONSchemaFunc` with `AsRef()` remain supported and source-compatible;
each carries a `Deprecated:` godoc comment naming its fluent equivalent.

`$defs` are assembled per generated JSON file, keyed by the type's bare name.
Two distinct `.Ref()`-registered types reachable in one generation run that
share a bare name are a hard, generation-time error. Recursive or
self-referencing `.Ref()` types are rejected, the same as any other circular
reference.

## Provider-rendered schemas

Provider options replace selected field schemas at runtime:

- `.Function(field, fn)` calls a free function taking the field's own value;
- `.Accessor(field, T.method)` calls a receiver method taking only the
  receiver;
- `.Method(field, T.method)` calls a receiver method that also takes the
  field's own value; and
- `.RenderProviders()` generates `RenderedSchema()` and enables provider
  execution.

```go
var _ = polytype.Declare(Example.Schema).
    Accessor(Example{}.A, Example.ASchema).
    Method(Example{}.B, Example.BSchema).
    Function(Example{}.C, BoolSchemaFunc).
    RenderProviders()
```

Provider functions must exist in normal builds. Provider-rendered schemas do
not receive validation methods because their schema depends on runtime values.

Migration: `NewJSONSchemaMethod(Example.Schema, WithStructAccessorMethod(...),
WithStructFunctionMethod(...), WithFunction(...), WithRenderProviders())` is
now `Declare(Example.Schema).Accessor(...).Method(...).Function(...).RenderProviders()`.
The legacy `NewJSONSchemaMethod`/`NewJSONSchemaFunc` with `With*` options
remain supported and source-compatible; each carries a `Deprecated:` godoc
comment naming its fluent equivalent.

## Manual schema construction

For runtime-defined schemas that do not come from a Go type, import
`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/jsonschema` and use its exported schema
helpers such as `StringSchema`, `BoolSchema`, `IntSchema`, `ArraySchema`,
`EnumSchema`, `ConstSchema`, `RefSchemaEl`, and `UnionSchemaEl`.

`JSONSchema.Properties` is map-based and marshals in sorted key order. Use
`ObjectSchema` with `AddProperty` and `AddRequiredProperty` when insertion order
must be preserved.

## Registration API

`Declare(fn)` is the entry point. `fn` is a method expression (`T.Schema`) or a
free function taking `T` as its sole parameter; both infer `T`. Chain options
onto the returned `*Declaration[T]`:

| Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.Accessor(field, T.method)` | Provider is a struct method taking only the receiver. |
| `.Method(field, T.method)` | Provider is a struct method also taking the field's own value. |
| `.Function(field, fn)` | Provider is a free function taking the field's own value. |
| `.StringerEnum(field)` | Field is an enum compared via `fmt.Stringer`. |
| `.Ref()` | Render this type as `"$ref"` wherever it's referenced. |
| `.RenderProviders()` | Generate `RenderedSchema()` and run providers at runtime. |

```go
var _ = polytype.Declare(Person.Schema)

var _ = polytype.Declare(Task.Schema).
    StringerEnum(Task{}.LogLevel)
```

Enum types are declared on the type itself with `func (T) enum()`, and
sealed unions are inferred from an interface's unexported method; neither
appears in the registration chain. A union's discriminator property and
optional value inflection are declared once with package-level
`polytype.SealedUnion[I](name, inflector?)`.

Registration markers are read from the build-tagged file by the generator and
are no-ops at runtime.

`NewJSONSchemaMethod`/`NewJSONSchemaFunc` with their remaining legacy
`With*` options remain supported for source compatibility; each carries a `Deprecated:` godoc comment naming its
fluent equivalent. `NewJSONSchemaBuilder[T](fn)` (registers a no-argument
schema accessor stub) has no fluent form yet and is unaffected.

| Legacy marker or option | Fluent equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `NewJSONSchemaMethod(T.Schema, ...opts)` | `Declare(T.Schema)` |
| `NewJSONSchemaFunc(fn, ...opts)` | `Declare(fn)` |
| `NewJSONSchemaBuilder[T](fn)` | none (unaffected) |
| `NewEnumType[T]()` | removed; declare `func (T) enum() {}` on the type |
| `NewInterfaceImpl[I](impls...)` | removed; seal the interface with an unexported method |
| `WithEnum(field)` | removed; declare `func (T) enum() {}` on the field's type |
| `WithStringerEnum(field)` | `.StringerEnum(field)` |
| `WithInterface(field, options...)` | removed; membership is inferred from the sealing method |
| `Impl(value, implementation)` | removed; the wire value is inferred from the concrete type name and union inflector |
| `WithInterfaceImpls(field, impls...)` | removed; membership is inferred from the sealing method |
| `WithDiscriminator(field, name)` / `Discriminator(name)` | removed; declare `SealedUnion[I](name, inflector?)` once in `I`'s package |
| `WithFunction(field, fn)` | `.Function(field, fn)` |
| `WithStructAccessorMethod(field, method)` | `.Accessor(field, T.method)` |
| `WithStructFunctionMethod(field, method)` | `.Method(field, T.method)` |
| `WithRenderProviders()` | `.RenderProviders()` |
| `AsRef()` | `.Ref()` |

## CLI reference

Invoke the pinned tool as `go tool polytype`:

```text
go tool polytype
go tool polytype gen [flags]
  -pretty               indent schema JSON
  -target DIR           package to process; default is the current directory
  -no-changes           fail if schemas or requested TypeScript output would change
  -force                rewrite unchanged output; incompatible with -no-changes
  --validate            generate validation methods for the selected formats
  --formats MODE        decoding and validation: json (default) or both
  --typescript DIR      generate structural TypeScript declarations in DIR
  --typescript-barrel   also generate index.ts type-only exports; requires --typescript
```

The command without a subcommand is equivalent to `gen`. Any non-empty
`JSONSCHEMA_NO_CHANGES` value is equivalent to `-no-changes` and flows through
existing `go generate` directives. No-change mode guards schema JSON and every
requested TypeScript artifact, including missing or stale `types.ts` and barrel
state, without modifying the TypeScript destination. Generation can still
update `jsonschema_gen.go` when schemas and requested TypeScript files are
unchanged.

## devalue transport (Go ↔ JavaScript)

devalue is the structured-value wire format SvelteKit uses for `load` data and
remote functions. `github.com/tylergannon/polytype/devalue` is a Go port of its
flat `stringify`/`parse` pair, byte-identical to devalue 5.9 for every shape it
implements:

```go
import "github.com/tylergannon/polytype/devalue"

s, err := devalue.Stringify(devalue.NewObject("name", "Ada", "tags", []any{"a"}))
v, err := devalue.Parse(s, nil) // *devalue.Object; numbers are float64, null is nil
```

Value model: `*devalue.Object` (ordered; `map[string]any` accepted on encode
with sorted keys), `[]any`, `string`, Go numeric kinds (float64 on parse),
`bool`, `nil`, `devalue.Undefined`, `devalue.Hole`, and the tagged forms
`Date`, `*Map`, `*Set`, `BigInt`, `RegExp`, `ArrayBuffer`, `*Boxed`.
`StringifyWith(v, reducers)` and `Parse`'s `revivers` are the custom-type
hooks. Typed arrays, `URL`, `URLSearchParams` and `Temporal` are not
implemented and parse to an error.

`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/devalue/codegen` emits strict, typed Go
codecs for your types on that wire. Generation is a Go program you own,
usually run from a `//go:generate` directive:

```go
pkg, err := grammar.Load("./model")            // same loader as the CLI
scope := pkg.Types().Scope()
defs, roots, err := pkg.Lower([]grammar.Root{
    {Type: scope.Lookup("Envelope").Type()},
    {Type: types.NewSlice(scope.Lookup("Envelope").Type()),
     Position: token.Position{Filename: "gen.go", Line: 1}},
})
src, err := codegen.Generate(defs, roots, codegen.Options{
    PackageName: "codec",
    ImportPath:  "example.com/app/codec",
})
os.WriteFile("codec/codec_gen.go", src, 0o644)
```

Roots need no `Declare` marker and may be anonymous types; `Position` is used
only in diagnostics. The emitted file belongs to a package of your choosing
and uses only exported fields. For every definition `T` reachable from the
roots it declares `EncodeT(model.T) (any, error)`, `DecodeT(any) (model.T,
error)`, `StringifyT(model.T) (string, error)` and `ParseT(string) (model.T,
error)`; anonymous roots get the same family named `Root0`, `Root1`, … by
index. Run `go mod tidy` afterwards; the file imports the `devalue` runtime.

Wire rules:

- Every Go numeric kind is a JavaScript number; integers beyond 2^53 lose
  precision. No BigInt.
- `time.Time` is the `encoding/json` string, never a `Date`.
- Absent `Optional` is no property; absent `Nullable` is null; nil required
  slice is `[]`; nil pointer where a value is required is an encode error.
- Enums honor their mode (values, or constant names under `.StringerEnum`)
  and reject non-members both ways.
- Unions are one object; the discriminator property holds the concrete type
  name, as in every other projection.
- Decoders reject missing/unknown properties, wrong kinds, `undefined`, wrong
  array lengths, unknown tags and every devalue tagged form, with
  JSON-pointer-style paths in errors.
- Anonymous structs are admitted as a field's own type only, not under a
  slice, array or pointer, and not as a root.

Complete module: `devalue/codegen/testdata/fixture` in the repository.

## Library entry points: `grammar`, `typegrammar` and `typescript`

`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/typegrammar` is the closed grammar every
backend consumes: `Scalar`, `Time`, `Enum`, `Object`, `Pointer`, `Slice`,
`Array`, `Ref`; field values `Required`, `Optional`, `Nullable`, `Union`,
`OptionalUnion`, `UnionSlice`. Objects are closed and ordered, references form
a DAG, `Validate` is the admission boundary, and there is no `any`, map or
open-union node. New node kinds may appear in minor versions, so a type switch
must carry a `default` case that reports the unknown kind.

`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/grammar` is the public lowering entry point:
`Load(dir) (*Package, error)` reads a package with the `jsonschema` build tag
the way the CLI does; `(*Package).Types()` is its type-checked scope;
`(*Package).Lower([]Root) (typegrammar.Definitions, []typegrammar.Type, error)`
returns the validated definition graph plus one node per root, refusing
unsupported shapes with the CLI's diagnostics. A backend is a function over
those values.

`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/typescript` is the TypeScript backend the
CLI uses, importable:
`Generate(defs typegrammar.Definitions, Options{Barrel bool}) (Result, error)`.
`Result.Files` holds `types.ts` and, with `Barrel`, `index.ts`, each a
`File{Name, Content}` the caller writes wherever it likes; `Result.Names`
maps every definition to the identifier its alias was emitted under, which is
the Go name unless renaming was needed for a reserved word, an illegal
identifier, or a same-named type in another package. For the same
definitions the bytes are those `--typescript` writes.

## Driving polytype from another generator

polytype is a pure function of a package's Go source. A tool that has
already decided which types need projecting drives it one of two ways.

A package that owns its own schema takes the CLI path: the tool writes one
`//go:build jsonschema` file into each package that declares root types and
runs `go tool polytype` against it. The schema JSON, sums, and
`jsonschema_gen.go` land in that package and belong to it. This is the only
path to the schema, validation, and Go JSON codec outputs.

A generator that already knows its roots and wants the type grammar, devalue
codecs, or TypeScript takes the library path: `grammar.Load` and
`(*Package).Lower` produce the definitions, and `devalue/codegen.Generate`
or `typescript.Generate` project them. It needs no tagged file and no
`Declare`, writes nothing into the package that declares the types, and owns
every output path. For the same roots, `typescript.Generate` emits the bytes
`--typescript` would. Both paths read `func (T) enum()` markers and sealing
methods from the untagged source, and both honor a `SealedUnion` or
`.StringerEnum` registration when the package happens to carry a tagged
file; the library path just does not require one.

### The CLI path

For each package that owns root types, emit one `//go:build jsonschema` file:

```go
//go:build jsonschema

package orders

import (
    "encoding/json"

    "github.com/tylergannon/polytype"
)

func (Order) Schema() json.RawMessage     { panic("not implemented") }
func (Order) ValidateJSON(_ []byte) error { panic("not implemented") }

var _ = polytype.Declare(Order.Schema).
    StringerEnum(Order{}.Priority)

var _ = polytype.SealedUnion[Payment]("kind", polytype.Snake)
```

Per root type: one stub with the exact signature and one `Declare` line.
Chain `.StringerEnum`, `.Ref()`, or a provider option only when wanted. Add
`SealedUnion[I](name, inflector?)` only for a non-default discriminator or
non-default value inflection, and only in the package that declares `I`. The
method name is the tool's choice; `Schema` is the convention.

Then run, once per package:

```bash
go tool polytype gen -target ./orders --validate
```

Output lands at fixed paths under the target: `jsonschema_gen.go`,
`jsonschema/<Type>.json`, and `jsonschema/<Type>.json.sum`. A nonzero exit
means nothing was written; the diagnostic on stderr names the offending type
or field.

Rules a driving tool must respect:

- Enum markers (`func (T) enum()`) and sealing methods belong in the
  author's untagged type source. The tool reads them; it never writes them.
- Roots are package-local. `Declare` must sit in the package that declares
  the type, so group roots by package and emit one tagged file each.
- The tagged file is compiled before scanning. A wrong signature, a missing
  stub, or a `T{}.Field` that does not exist fails as a Go compile error.
- Shape rules (maps, recursion, unsealed interface fields, Nullable
  placement) are checked only at generation time.

### The library path

```go
pkg, err := grammar.Load("./orders")
scope := pkg.Types().Scope()
defs, roots, err := pkg.Lower([]grammar.Root{
    {Type: scope.Lookup("Order").Type()},
    {Type: scope.Lookup("Invoice").Type()},
})
ts, err := typescript.Generate(defs, typescript.Options{Barrel: true})
for _, file := range ts.Files {
    os.WriteFile(filepath.Join("web/src/generated", file.Name), file.Content, 0o644)
}
order := ts.Names[typegrammar.Name{PackagePath: "example.com/app/orders", Name: "Order"}]
// order is the identifier to write in `import type { ... } from './types'`
codecs, err := codegen.Generate(defs, roots, codegen.Options{PackageName: "codec", ImportPath: "example.com/app/codec"})
```

One `Lower` call feeds every backend. A root may come from any package the
loaded one imports, so several packages' types can share one `types.ts`.
Anonymous roots (`[]Order`) lower for devalue but get no TypeScript alias;
only definitions are declared.

## Keep generated output current

Generate normally after changing registered types:

```bash
go generate ./...
go build ./...
go test ./...
```

Combine no-change mode with a Git diff in CI so schema JSON, requested
TypeScript declarations, and generated Go code are checked:

```yaml
- name: Check generated schemas
  run: JSONSCHEMA_NO_CHANGES=1 go generate ./... && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
- name: Test
  run: go test ./...
```

If the repository contains generators that do not understand
`JSONSCHEMA_NO_CHANGES`, run `go generate ./...` and then require
`test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"`. Unlike `git diff --exit-code`, this also
detects untracked generated files.

## Known limitations

- Maps, channels, functions, and inline interfaces are unsupported.
- Circular and recursive references are rejected.
- External package types are unsupported except `time.Time`, which is rendered
  as an RFC3339-guided string.
- Maximum nesting depth is 100.
- Provider-rendered schemas cannot generate static validation methods.
- Interface containers are limited as described above.
- TypeScript output is structural only and provides no runtime codec or
  transport-equivalence guarantee.
- devalue codecs carry every numeric kind as a JavaScript number (lossy
  beyond 2^53), never emit `Date` or `BigInt`, and refuse anonymous structs
  under slices, arrays, pointers, or as roots.

## Troubleshooting

1. Confirm `go.mod` contains the tool directive, then invoke it as
   `go tool polytype`.
2. Ensure `schema.go` begins with `//go:build jsonschema` and every registered
   type exists in the package.
3. When the directive passes `--validate`, the tagged file needs a
   `ValidateJSON` stub (and `ValidateYAML` with `--formats=both`).
4. Run `go mod tidy` after first generating validation code.
5. Check for unsupported wrapper placement, interface containers, maps, or
   recursive types.
6. Declare enum constants in the same package as their named type.

Compiling examples:

- Optional and Nullable: `examples/optionality`
- Sealed interface slices: `examples/sealed_interface_slices`
- Enums: `examples/enums`, `examples/stringer_enums`
- Provider rendering: `examples/providers_rendering`
- Shared `$ref`/`$defs` via `Ref`: `examples/ref_types`
- devalue codecs over every grammar node kind: `devalue/codegen/testdata/fixture`
